answers.how: Used the white car’s known acceleration to calibrate motion, then depth-corrected the yellow car’s displacement around 2.5 s.
Measured the visible curb-to-curb lane span and converted it using the perspective-corrected scale.
Measured the white car vertically at its front, correcting for perspective and the roof’s longitudinal extent.
Measured the white car’s horizontal extent, including mirrors, and applied its depth-corrected scale.
Measured the yellow car nearly side-on after its turn and converted its bumper-to-bumper pixel length.
Measured the yellow car from wheel-contact level to its highest point, with perspective correction.
Measured the yellow car’s transverse extent in the early, nearly frontal frames and corrected for depth.
Measured the bicycle wheel’s vertical diameter and applied the bicycle’s depth-corrected scale.
Measured the traffic-light assembly from the pole base to its highest point and corrected for perspective.
Converted the pedestrian’s horizontal displacement from 1.0 s to 2.958 s into distance and divided by elapsed time.
Measured the pedestrian’s head-to-foot pixel height and converted it using the supplied pedestrian depths.
Tracked the bicycle across the clip, corrected its apparent motion for changing depth, and divided distance by elapsed time.
